t: Before completing the post-shakedown availability of the Ford class aircraft carrier designated CVN–79, the Secretary of the Navy shall ensure that the aircraft carrier is capable of operating and deploying with the F–35C aircraft.

fable.w: This section only directs a federal official, the Secretary of the Navy, to ensure an aircraft carrier has a certain capability before a milestone. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. There is no real tempting reading, since the only actor is inside the government.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Navy shall ensure that the aircraft carrier is capable of operating and deploying with the F–35C aircraft.

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a technical readiness requirement on the Secretary of the Navy regarding a specific aircraft carrier. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or input from any party outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). The decision-making process described is internal to the Department of the Navy.
qwen_block.s: Before completing the post-shakedown availability of the Ford class aircraft carrier designated CVN–79, the Secretary of the Navy shall ensure that the aircraft carrier is capable of operating and deploying with the F–35C aircraft.

opus.w: This section only requires the Secretary of the Navy to make sure CVN-79 can operate and deploy with the F-35C aircraft before its post-shakedown availability is completed. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted or given a role in the decision. The pre-decision condition might look procedural, but it never involves anyone outside the federal government, so it is not participation.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** One might read this as "participation" because it sets a condition the Secretary must meet before a federal decision, which is completing the carrier's post-shakedown availability. That reading fails because nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, asked for comment or given a right to sue. This is a technical requirement handled entirely inside the Navy.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a readiness requirement on the Secretary of the Navy regarding the operational capability of a specific aircraft carrier. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any party outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private companies). The decision-making process described is internal to the Department of the Navy.
qwen_chat.s: Before completing the post-shakedown availability of the Ford class aircraft carrier designated CVN–79, the Secretary of the Navy shall ensure that the aircraft carrier is capable of operating and deploying with the F–35C aircraft.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that ensuring the carrier is capable of operating with F-35C aircraft involves coordination with the Air Force or Lockheed Martin (the manufacturer), which are outside entities. However, the text itself does not mandate any consultation, coordination, or participation with these external parties; it simply sets a performance standard for the Navy's internal readiness process. The actors explicitly mentioned are the Secretary of the Navy (federal official) and the aircraft/carrier (equipment). There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
